claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can reduce the coefficient of friction of a high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can reduce the wear rate of a high-entropy alloy.
Forming an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer can reduce the coefficient of friction of a high-entropy alloy.
Forming an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer can reduce the wear rate of a high-entropy alloy.
The proposed nanohierarchical treatment reduces the contact area between opposing surfaces.
The proposed nanohierarchical treatment increases surface hardness.
The proposed nanohierarchical treatment promotes formation of a self-lubricating tribofilm.
Reduced contact area, increased surface hardness, and self-lubricating tribofilm formation improve the tribological behavior of high-entropy alloys.
The treatment will reduce coefficient of friction by at least 30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will reduce wear rate by at least 25% relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment remains effective over a service-temperature range from -20°C to 200°C.
The magnitudes of friction and wear reduction depend on alloy composition, surface roughness, and contact pressure.
